text:
marta: quick heads-up — during today’s canary we saw a low-priority tenant get routed to the debug lane and two requests ended up sampled with PII not redacted. 

josh: ugh. which sampler policy was active?

marta: `fallback_policy: tenant_priority` + burst fill behavior. when Dedicated pool overloaded, requests from lower priority buckets fell back to the inspect-capable path.

navin: can you paste the small repro?

marta: pasted logs: ```
[2026-03-21T16:12:03Z] route=/v1/generate tenant=tenant-42 priority=low -> routed to debug-proxy
[2026-03-21T16:12:03Z] sampler.sampled=true sample_reason=fallback_tenant_priority config_hash=ab12
[2026-03-21T16:12:04Z] payload="customer cc 4242-xxxx-xxxx-1234"
```

elaine: thanks for flagging. we intentionally allow debug-proxy to short-circuit redaction for inspect; but we assumed fallback kept redaction on. bug.

sam: is this because fallback preserves sampling decision but not redact policy? iirc we decoupled `sample` vs `inspect_allowed` to avoid perf hits.

josh: yep — sampler returns {sampled: true, path: debug} but redact flag came from original route metadata which got lost when routing layer rewrote the envelope.

navin: immediate mitigation: patch routing to carry redact=true as part of the fallback envelope. low-risk hotfix. we should also add a circuit to never enable debug-without-redact unless tenant explicitly opted-in.

marta: agree. also think we need console UX change: when a tenant is low-priority and fallback routing is enabled, show an "inspect-risk" badge on the tenant config and a per-route toggle: "allow debug inspect on fallback" (default off).

elaine: UX note — product asked for quick visual on rollout pages: when doing canaries, highlight any routes where fallback could cause redact=false. small red triangle + tooltip should work.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary/2026-03-21T16:15 started by @marta — tag=canary-sampler-fix.

sam: proposal for config shape (very small): ```json
{
  "sampler": {
    "default_rate": 0.01,
    "fallback_policy": "tenant_priority",
    "fallback_meta": {
      "preserve_redact": true,
      "allow_inspect_on_fallback": false
    }
  }
}
```

josh: +1 to preserve_redact default true. if allow_inspect_on_fallback is true we must require: tenant.has_inspect_consent = true AND UI displays granted permissions with timestamp.

navin: telemetry ask: emit an event when fallback routes set inspect=true so we can alert on accidental exposures. event fields: tenant, route, original_priority, dest, redact_preserved(bool), request_id.

marta: also add a dashboard card: "fallback inspect attempts" with a small sampling heatmap (time + tenant). default retention 30d.

elaine: operational runbook: if an exposure is detected, a) revoke inspect capability for that canary immediately, b) mark affected requests for audit, c) notify security on-call. we should document in release notes.

sam: follow-ups: (1) hotfix routing envelope to carry redact flag (owner: navin, ETA today), (2) console badge + toggle (owner: elaine, ETA 2d), (3) telemetry event + dashboard (owner: marta, ETA 3d), (4) runbook paragraph (owner: josh, ETA tomorrow).

marta: I'll attach a short repro snippet and add unit tests to sampler integration.

josh: thanks. can we also add a CI smoke in infra that simulates fallback during burst so this doesn't regress?

navin: yes — will add a small e2e that flips a pool to 0 capacity and asserts redact preserved.

elaine: leaving a note for product: we need language for tenant consent UI if they want opt-in inspect on fallback — legal needs to review wording.

marta: ok locking on owners. thanks all :thumbsup:
